# guard-act-s3062-reported-text-2026-05-11
- **URL:** https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3062rs/pdf/BILLS-119s3062rs.pdf · **Accessed:** 2026-09-16 · **For:** v2→v3 response round, slice L
- **What it establishes:** PRIMARY. S. 3062 (GUARD Act), 119th Cong., Reported in Senate, Calendar No. 406; introduced Oct 28, 2025 (Hawley + 19 cosponsors listed); "MAY 11, 2026 Reported by Mr. GRASSLEY, with an amendment [Strike out all after the enacting clause and insert the part printed in italic]". 28 pp., read locally WITH FONT ANALYSIS. CRITICAL: the PDF prints TWO texts. Pages 1–13 (roman type) are the INTRODUCED text, which the committee STRUCK. Pages 14–27 (italic type) are the committee substitute, which is the operative reported text. The sentences the editorial review quoted — Sec. 5(a) "each individual accessing an artificial intelligence chatbot" and Sec. 3(5) "(A) a government-issued identification; or (B) any other commercially reasonable method" — are in the STRUCK text (pp. 4, 8). In the REPORTED substitute: (1) the account and age-verification mandates apply to "AI companion[s]" only (Sec. 5(a), (b), p. 21–22); (2) Sec. 3(5) lists five example methods — (A) "a verified form of identification"; (B) age information from a financial-institution account derived from verified ID; (C) same from an operating-system account; (D) same from an app-store account; (E) "any other commercially reasonable method that can determine whether a user is an adult" (pp. 16–17); (3) Sec. 3(7) defines "verified form of identification" as government-issued ID OR "another form of identification corroborated by authentic documentation" (p. 18). Government ID is therefore ONE PERMISSIBLE METHOD, not required, in both versions. Self-attestation insufficient: process "does not solely require a user to confirm that the user is not a minor or to insert the user’s birth date" (Sec. 3(6)(B), p. 17). Existing accounts frozen on the effective date until verified; new accounts verified at creation; periodic re-verification (Sec. 5(b)(1)–(3), pp. 21–22). Data minimization/retention/no-sale clause: Sec. 5(b)(5) (p. 23–24). What still reaches ALL chatbots, general-purpose included: the definition of "artificial intelligence chatbot" (Sec. 3(2): any service that "generates responses that are not fully predetermined" and accepts open-ended natural-language input, excluding narrow-purpose bots), the two new crimes in 18 U.S.C. § 91 (Sec. 4), and the non-human/non-professional disclosures (Sec. 5(c)). The "AI companion" definition (Sec. 3(1)) is functional, not product-based, and its limb "engages in interactions involving emotional disclosures from the user" could arguably reach a general-purpose assistant; that is my reading, not a finding of any source. Minors barred from AI companions (Sec. 6). Civil penalty up to $250,000 per violation; AG and state AG enforcement (Sec. 7). Effective 180 days after enactment (Sec. 9).
- **Key passages:**
  - REPORTED Sec. 5(a) (p. 21, italic): "A covered entity shall require each individual accessing an AI companion to make a user account in order to use or otherwise interact with the AI companion."
  - STRUCK Sec. 5(a) (p. 8, roman): "A covered entity shall require each individual accessing an artificial intelligence chatbot to make a user account in order to use ..."
  - REPORTED Sec. 3(1) (p. 15): "‘‘AI companion’’ means an artificial intelligence chatbot that, in a manner that simulates a sustained interpersonal relationship or emotional interaction with the user— (A) exhibits persistent responses suggesting affection or attachment directed toward the user or engages in interactions involving emotional disclosures from the user; or (B) presents at least one persistent identity, persona, or character and holds itself out as a sentient being, fictional character, or social entity."
  - REPORTED Sec. 3(5) (p. 16): "a method that, whether alone or in conjunction with other age verification measures, can, with reasonable certainty, determine whether the user of an interactive computer service or software application is an adult, such as— (A) a verified form of identification; ... (E) any other commercially reasonable method that can determine whether a user is an adult."
  - REPORTED Sec. 3(7) (p. 18): "‘‘verified form of identification’’ means— (A) a government-issued identification that can determine the adult status of the person identified; or (B) another form of identification corroborated by authentic documentation that can, with reasonable certainty, determine the adult status of the person identified."
  - REPORTED Sec. 5(b)(1) (p. 21): "With respect to each user account of an AI companion that exists as of the effective date of this Act, a covered entity shall— (A) on that date, freeze the account; (B) in order to restore the functionality of the account, require verification that the user is an adult using a reasonable age verification process"
  - REPORTED Sec. 5(b)(3) (p. 22): "A covered entity shall periodically re-verify previously verified user accounts using a reasonable age verification process"
  - REPORTED Sec. 5(b)(5) (p. 23): "limit collection of personal data to that which is minimally necessary to verify a user’s adult status or maintain compliance with this Act"; "(D) shall retain such data for no longer than is reasonably necessary ..."; "(E) may not share with, transfer to, or sell to, any other entity such data."
  - REPORTED Sec. 3(3) (p. 16): "‘‘covered entity’’ means any person who makes publicly available to end consumers an artificial intelligence chatbot."
- **Reliability:** Primary (GPO). The roman/italic distinction was verified by extracting font names per page (DeVinne vs DeVinne-Italic); plain-text extraction loses it, which is how a reader can quote the struck text by mistake. Line numbers were stripped in my extraction, so give page cites, not line cites.
- **Relevance to this project:** L5 CONFIRMED WITH MAJOR CORRECTION. Status correct (reported by Senate Judiciary, Calendar No. 406, May 11, 2026; no floor action found as of 2026-09-16). But any sentence saying the reported GUARD Act makes every chatbot user create an account and verify age is WRONG for the reported text; that was the introduced bill. The accurate claim: the bill as introduced would have, and 20 senators sponsored that version; the committee narrowed it to AI companions on April 30, 2026.
